Messages.Author: pallando
Messages.Body:
to play cardinal sin: insubordination i need a ready priscus, cardinal, or
archbishop. can a vampire that has just completed combat with another sabbat
vampire play this card? or do i have to play it with a wake or another
untapped vampired with the appropriate title?

something similar: elder kindred network. i assume that i need a ready and
untapped ventrue vampire to play this, correct?

thanks

pallando

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 12 Oct 2000, pallando wrote:

> to play cardinal sin: insubordination i need a ready priscus, cardinal, or
> archbishop. can a vampire that has just completed combat with another sabbat
> vampire play this card?

You could (since there are no restrictions that it must be played by
another vampire), but they would need to be untapped, or under the
influence of an untap-style ability (e.g. Wake). Were you to have been
rushed, for example, you may well be untapped and able to use it.

> or do i have to play it with a wake or another
> untapped vampired with the appropriate title?

Both perfectly possible.

> something similar: elder kindred network. i assume that i need a ready and
> untapped ventrue vampire to play this, correct?

Yes, it does. Only ready vampires can play reaction cards, unless
otherwise specified. It needs a Ventrue because it requires Ventrue.

It also needs to be untapped *OR* awake (e.g. Wake etc.)

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 13 Oct 2000, pallando wrote:

> thanks for the answer. i suspected this. unfortunately this renders cardinal
> sin: insubordination nearly useless.

It was already vaguely bad anyway.

Not having a Wake to play the cards you want, or having all tapped
vampires, is a Bad Thing (tm) however.

For instance, this could be funny combat defence in a Derange/Sacrifice
deck (which do exist). A few Wakes would not be a bad price to pay.
